paper.title: Algorithm 761: Scattered-data surface fitting that has the accuracy of a cubic polynomial
paper.venue: ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software 22(3), 362-371 (CALGO Algorithm 761)
paper.url: https://netlib.org/toms/761.gz (ACM article not read: the DL returns 403 to automated fetch)

code.commit: netlib TOMS archive 761.gz, a shell archive of driver.f, src.f, tripack.f and the authors' result file res
code.note: Unshar (it only creates files; read it first). Build driver.f, src.f (SDBI3P, SDSF3P) and tripack.f (Renka's TRIPACK, included). The driver reads no input and writes its result to a file named res. Fortran 77, REAL (single) precision: expect gfortran -std=legacy.

claim.location: The authors' shipped result file res, Part 1 'Program Check for SDBI3P', 'Calculation by points': the left table ZI1(XI,YI) of interpolated values on a 6 x 5 grid for the 30 data points of the driver. Registered: six interior grid points that are not data points. The same file also shows non-zero 'differences' DZI (up to 0.57) although the driver comment says all DZI elements are expected to be zero; that discrepancy is recorded here as a thing to watch, not as the claim.
claim.metric: the interpolated value ZI1 printed (two decimals) by the driver for each registered grid point

tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. The shipped values are printed to two decimals from single-precision arithmetic, so a correct rebuild matches to 0.01 plus one unit of rounding; 0.011 absolute allows that and is about 0.03% of the typical value of 20. Not to be loosened after any run.

cost.data_size: None: the 30 data points are in the driver.
cost.data_licence: No data. Includes Renka's TRIPACK (ACM, Algorithm 751); licence not stated in the archive.

why: A 1996 scattered-data package ships its own result table for a 30-point problem. The interpolation needs the full code (Delaunay triangulation, gradient estimation, bivariate polynomials), so the values test whether this old single-precision Fortran still reproduces its published numbers.
